bugs.summary: Title, branch and diff-excludes rule checks run a repo admin's regular expression with the backtracking JavaScript engine against text the pull request author controls, so a pattern like `(a+)+$` or `\d+\d+\d+x` with a crafted title, branch or added line hangs the triage worker (catastrophic backtracking).
bugs.evidence: rule-checks.ts:56 `!new RegExp(check.pattern).test(facts.title)`, :61 same on `facts.branch`, :70 `diffHits(files, new RegExp(check.pattern))` tested per added line at :32. Patterns come from the tenant check pack: packages/triage-contracts/src/check-pack.ts:405-409 `pattern()` only checks `new RegExp(source)` compiles (outside the diff), max 200 chars. At base no pattern was ever matched (PR body: never evaluated). Fix #155 replaces all three with `RE2JS.compile(check.pattern)` (linear time) and rejects lookaround/backreferences at pack save.

bugs.summary: The paths-together rule puts the author-controlled changed file paths into its reason, which the author comment posts raw (only evidence is wrapped in inline code), so a file named e.g. `@someone.md` or containing markdown link syntax mentions or links from Triage's comment.
bugs.evidence: rule-checks.ts:53 `reason: failed ? `changes ${changed.join(", ")} without ...`` where `changed` are PR file paths; render.ts:344 posts `- ${c.reason}` raw and only `c.evidence.map(inlineCode)`. The PR states 'Evidence in the author comment posts as inline code'. Fix #193: 'The paths-together rule now puts the changed paths in its evidence instead of its reason.'

bugs.summary: A rule check that comes back unconfirmed (branch unknown, or a clean diff-excludes scan with unscanned additions) with nothing else failing leaves the pull request in ready-monitoring with next step 'Review and merge' and no maintainer step, while the merge verdict says not recommended; a decided model pass also ignores it.
bugs.evidence: rule-checks.ts:59 and :72 return failed:null, so evaluateRuleChecks pushes an unconfirmed machine check but no finding; checks.ts finish() derives state only from findings ('ready-monitoring'). render.ts:288-290 unconfirmedSteps gives a step only for conflicts or model checks, so nextStep falls through to 'Review and merge' (:296-298); render.ts:412 judged path counts only evaluated (model) checks as unconfirmed. mergeVerdict (:369-370) does list 'Not confirmed: ...', so the outputs contradict. Later commit 383fe483 fixed the same gap: 'A decided pass with any unconfirmed rule is Unsure' (checks.some instead of evaluated.checks).

rejected.was: original: match path globs in linear time (glob.ts:1, :3-8)
rejected.why: Not introduced: glob.ts is moved verbatim from checks.ts (base 89651ab3 checks.ts:120-127), where it was already applied to tenant-written `forbiddenGlobs` (base checks.ts:246, check-pack.ts:361). The polynomial backtracking and the unescaped `?` predate this PR; fix #194 addresses pre-existing code.

rejected.was: round2 (1): rule evaluation nested inside an outer conditional block (checks.ts:249)
rejected.why: The enclosing block is the `else` of `facts.state === "closed"` (checks.ts:197); every check is skipped for a closed PR by design.

rejected.was: round2 (4): failedStep falls back to raw `Fix custom-n` when sources lack the rule (render.ts:262-268)
rejected.why: Rule checks are only evaluated when a pack exists (checks.ts:249), and finish() always sets sources = classificationSources(pack) which includes every rule row, so the lookup always hits.
Speculation: sources is only built by classificationSources (checks.ts:132), which now always returns `rules`; no persisted or external sources shape is rendered.

rejected.was: round2 (1): addedLines line numbers drift on CRLF or malformed hunk headers
rejected.why: Speculation: CRLF rows still start with '+', ' ' or '-'; GitHub patches always carry valid hunk headers.

rejected.was: round2 (2): path list or file list may be capped/incomplete so path and diff rules pass
rejected.why: directors.ts addFiles pages github_list_pr_files until `next` is undefined and errors on a stuck offset; later pages without patches leave patch undefined, which unscanned() reports as unconfirmed. Any GitHub-side cap is pre-existing and shared with the catalog paths check.

rejected.was: round2 (many): unknown `additions` treated as zero, so an unscanned file passes (rule-checks.ts:39)
rejected.why: Speculation: fileFacts keeps GitHub's `additions`, which the files API always returns as a count; no producer omits it.

rejected.was: round2 (many): `facts.paths ?? []` makes missing paths pass paths-unchanged / paths-together
rejected.why: assembleItem (facts.ts) always sets `paths` from the file list and degrades the item with an error when files could not be read; paths is never absent at evaluation. Same pattern as the pre-existing catalog paths check.

rejected.was: round2 (many): `facts.files ?? []` makes diff-excludes pass when files are missing
rejected.why: Same as paths: assembleItem always sets `files` or returns an error item, so files are never absent.

rejected.was: round2 (2): min-approvals passes when approvals is undefined
rejected.why: PrFacts.approvals is a required number, always set by buildFacts (reviewersWith(...).length).

rejected.was: round2 (2): diff evidence silently capped at five hits
rejected.why: Intended: MAX_DIFF_HITS bounds the evidence; the check still fails and names the rule.

rejected.was: round2 (1): results keep raw `custom-n` in the `check` field
rejected.why: `check` is the internal key the actions and sources lookups use; the PR names the rule in `reason`, which is what the comment and merge reasons show.
Throw part is wrong: check-pack.ts pattern() rejects patterns that do not compile when the pack is parsed. The ReDoS part of these findings matches b1.
